headline: Four weeks of progressive volume gain are confirmed, but today's aerobic efficiency — easy effort at notably lower HR than the prior block — is the real signal worth tracking.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Your aerobic base is responding. Easy-run HR has dropped meaningfully across comparable efforts over the last four weeks, which is a concrete physiological marker — not noise. That shift, combined with a sustained volume increase, suggests the recent training block is having the intended effect. The 20-week streak matching your personal best is context, but the efficiency data is the more useful signal right now.

The June 27th threshold effort remains the standout data point from the recent window — a genuinely high-quality session that anchors your current fitness ceiling. Today's 18 km at easy effort lands well as a volume accumulation run: distance without unnecessary cost. The pattern of mixing one hard effort per week with aerobic volume work is producing coherent load distribution.

Strength frequency dropped slightly in the recent block. Not a concern at this stage, but worth keeping an eye on — five sessions across four weeks is on the lower end of what this athlete typically sustains, and strength continuity matters for injury resilience at the distances you're building toward.
watch_items: Watch whether the easy-run HR trend continues downward — if so, it confirms genuine aerobic adaptation rather than day-to-day variance
Monitor whether strength frequency recovers to its prior level over the coming two weeks
Pay attention to how back-to-back run days feel as weekly volume continues building — durability under fatigue is the relevant test now, not single-session performance
The threshold session from late June set a high bar — notice whether efforts at similar intensity feel harder or easier as the block progresses

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 145 km vs 125 km prior block (+16%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 146 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 7 vs 6 runs)
